finding.claim: Broken authorization on the ban endpoint. require_admin() denies by calling abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. The ban() handler wraps that call in `except Exception`, which catches the exception and only logs a warning. Execution then continues to do_ban(uid), so any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users. The check fails open.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sends POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation.

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST with an attacker-controlled uid.
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block.
For a non-admin, abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, which is an Exception subclass.
Only a log.warning is emitted, with no re-raise and no return.
do_ban(uid) runs and the handler returns ok=True.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is correct in itself, and the unban route at line 26 calls it without a try block, so it is enforced there. No other decorator, before_request hook or middleware exists in the codebase. The exception handler defeats the only check on the ban route. The log line at admin.py:19 also writes the user-controlled name field, which is a minor log-injection risk.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 but its exception is swallowed by `except Exception` at admin.py:18; no decorator, before_request hook or middleware exists in the code
verdict.reason: admin.py:17 calls require_admin, which raises via abort(403) at line 11, but `except Exception` at line 18 only logs (line 19) with no re-raise or return, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for non-admins, unlike unban at line 26, which is unguarded by try.
